key_insight: ENGINE combines low-variance subspace updates with high-dimensional corrections to improve memory-efficient, zeroth-order LLM fine-tuning.
engineering_relevance: It transfers variational multiscale ideas from computational mechanics to optimization, treating parameter subspaces as coupled coarse and fine scales.
method: Adapt static Variational MultiScale theory to dynamic optimization.
Use a multigrid-style V-cycle to alternate between coarse and fine parameter spaces.
Inject high-dimensional information into low-dimensional sampling to reduce variance and correct curvature-induced bias.
evidence_signal: On standard LLM benchmarks, the abstract reports higher accuracy and faster convergence than existing ZO methods, with up to 2.61× speed-up in forward passes and no additional peak memory overhead.
watch_item: Theoretical guarantees depend on assumptions, and the abstract does not specify benchmark-level gains or wall-clock speed-ups.
paper_title: ENGINE: Endogenous Variational MultiScale Optimization for Zeroth-Order LLM Fine-Tuning
